title: ₹1 Lakh Ka Gold Set Bika: Jeweller Ki Jeb Mein Kitna Gaya?
description: Reasoning: jewellery shops are one of the most visible dream businesses in Indian towns, and everyone has bought gold at least once, so the topic is deeply relatable. The hidden-charges angle (making charges, wastage) is both an insider secret and a useful consumer tip, which drives saves and shares.
text:
**HISAAB FACT SHEET: Where a jeweller really makes money on a ₹1 lakh purchase**
Prepared 3 Nov 2026. Figures are mostly FY26 or early FY27. I could not find a verified net-profit figure for a small independent jeweller. All big-company numbers are from listed chains (Titan, Kalyan).

**1. THE CORE IDEA: the gold itself earns almost nothing**
- A jeweller usually makes no profit on the gold itself. The gold flows through at cost, so money comes from how they change it in between. [https://thedailybrief.zerodha.com/p/margin-crush-in-a-gold-rush]
- Bullion carries almost no margin. As Titan ramped up bullion sales, its gross margin fell by 600 basis points year on year. [https://thedailybrief.zerodha.com/p/margin-crush-in-a-gold-rush]
- Coins and bars: gold coins carry a 1-3% making charge and bars 1-5%. [https://www.ipomarket.in/news/gold-making-charges-explained-india]
- Coins yield lower profit margins than jewellery, so the shift to coins has constrained Titan's overall margin growth. [https://www.marketscreener.com/news/indian-jeweller-titan-posts-slower-sales-as-surge-in-gold-prices-dent-demand-ce7d5bddde8ff127]

**2. MAKING CHARGES (the main earner on plain gold)**
- Plain gold jewellery: making charges add roughly 6-15% of gold value, and gross margin lands at 12-13%. [https://thedailybrief.zerodha.com/p/margin-crush-in-a-gold-rush]
- On a ₹1 lakh plain-gold sale, a 12-13% gross margin is ₹12,000-₹13,000. This is my arithmetic on the sourced percentage. It is gross margin, before rent, staff and interest.
- Branded chains: Tanishq, Malabar and Kalyan charge 12-20% on most pieces. [https://www.ipomarket.in/news/gold-making-charges-explained-india]
- Typical range across India is 8-25% of gold value, depending on design and type of jeweller. [https://goldmap.in/learn/gold-making-charges-explained] Other sources quote 3-25% or 5-25%, so treat the range as wide and varying by city and jeweller.
- Flat-rate method: plain pieces are ₹250-500 per gram, while intricate work is billed as 8-22% wastage. [https://www.kishnajewellersllp.in/guides/gold-making-charges-explained]
- Worked bill example: on ₹1,80,000 of metal, 12% making (₹21,600) plus 4% wastage (₹7,200) adds ₹28,800, which is 16% over gold value before tax. [https://www.krishniahchetty.co/jewellery-guide/buying-and-price-guide/ckc-guide-gold-making-charges]
- The BIS hallmarking charge is ₹45 per article. [https://www.krishniahchetty.co/jewellery-guide/buying-and-price-guide/ckc-guide-gold-making-charges]
- Resale: when you sell or exchange, you are paid for gold content only, by weight and purity, not the making charges you paid. [https://apexinfluence.in/jewellery-making-charges]

**3. WASTAGE (part real cost, part margin)**
- Hand-made jewellery once lost 3-5% of gold in melting and casting, so wastage was a real cost. [https://www.ipomarket.in/news/gold-making-charges-explained-india]
- Modern machine-made jewellery has near-zero actual wastage, but jewellers still charge it. [https://www.ipomarket.in/news/gold-making-charges-explained-india]
- Typical wastage charged: 3-10% in India. [https://www.ipomarket.in/news/gold-making-charges-explained-india] Other sources say 5-7%, and 2-8% (GoldMeter). It varies by jeweller. Some jewellers, particularly in South India, bill wastage separately from making charges. [https://goldmap.in/learn/gold-making-charges-explained]
- Insider line: on a machine-made piece, a high wastage charge is usually just margin by another name. [https://apexinfluence.in/jewellery-making-charges]

**4. PLAIN GOLD vs STUDDED: where the margin sits**
- Studded jewellery: the diamond carries its own mark-up and the gold still earns making charges. Gross margins on a heavily studded mix can run as high as the mid-thirties. [https://thedailybrief.zerodha.com/p/margin-crush-in-a-gold-rush]
- A blog by a diamond institute puts it differently: 25-30% gross margin on studded versus 10-12% on plain gold. [https://www.jkdiamondsinstitute.com/blog/what-kalyan-jewellers-%E2%82%B933-000-crore-fy26-results-mean-for-every-small-and-medium-jeweller-in-india] This is a secondary source. The Zerodha figures above are better for the script.
- Making-charge ranges: studded (diamond + gold) is 18-40%, against 5-10% for plain bangles. [https://www.ipomarket.in/news/gold-making-charges-explained-india]
- Studded share of sales is the profit lever. Kalyan's studded share held flat at 31.2%, while Titan's slipped from 34% to 31%. [https://thedailybrief.zerodha.com/p/margin-crush-in-a-gold-rush]
- Record gold prices push the mix toward plain gold and coins. Rising gold prices shift the mix toward coins and reduce the percentage margin of studded jewellery. [https://financepulse.ai/earnings-calls/titan-company-q3-fy26-13-feb/]

**5. OLD-GOLD EXCHANGE DEDUCTION**
- Exchange is huge. Titan's Q3 FY26 earnings-call summary credits exchange programmes with about 50% of its contribution. [https://financepulse.ai/earnings-calls/titan-company-q3-fy26-13-feb/] This is a third-party call summary, so verify it against the transcript.
- Standard deduction: a melting or refining charge of typically 2-5%. [https://www.iifl.com/blogs/gold-loan/what-is-gold-buyback-policy-jewellers] A different IIFL page says 1-3%. [https://www.iifl.com/blogs/gold-loan/gold-jewellery-exchange-offer-at-jewellers]
- Buy-back price: national chains typically buy back at 90-96% of the declared rate, and remelting loss is usually 2-4%. [https://www.terra-insight.com/insights/old-gold-exchange-new-purchase-reconciliation-section-194ia-india/]
- Competitor claims are much higher: a Nagpur jeweller says most jewellers deduct 10-20% of the weight before crediting. [https://londejewellers.com/gold-exchange-nagpur] This is a marketing claim from a "0% deduction" shop, so treat it as the extreme end.
- Some shops advertise 0% deduction on old gold exchange. [https://www.indriya.com/gold-exchange] The deduction is clearly negotiable and varies by shop and city.
- Stones are not paid for. Jewellers deduct 2-5% for wear and meltdown loss, and stone weight is not valued. [https://www.unwindlogic.com/hidden-charges-in-gold-jewellery-complete-guide/]
- Tax detail: if old jewellery is resold as second-hand with its design intact, 3% GST applies only on the margin between resale price and buy-back cost. [https://www.terra-insight.com/insights/old-gold-exchange-new-purchase-reconciliation-section-194ia-india/]

**6. TAX ON THE BILL**
- Gold jewellery carries 3% GST on the total price, including gold, making charges and gemstones. [https://www.ujjivansfb.bank.in/banking-blogs/gold-loan/how-gold-price-is-calculated-by-jewellers]
- Conflict: some blogs say 5% GST applies to making charges. [https://loovi.in/blog/gold-jewellery-making-charges-india] I could not confirm this on an official source, so use 3% only after checking CBIC.
- GST is a pass-through to the government, not the jeweller's earnings.
